poles: You took the loan, you pay it / why should the plumber pay for your degree

reader_anchor.opening_prose: You are seven years old. Your friend borrows your favorite red crayon. He breaks it in half. He says sorry. You still have two halves of a red crayon and no whole one. You remember the feeling: sorry does not fix the crayon. Someone still has to get a new one. That someone is either you, or your friend, or your mom who was not even in the room. You did not know the word 'ledger' yet. But you knew the math: the broken crayon is real. The cost does not disappear because someone says sorry. You learned it in your hand. Later, they taught you to stop counting. They said 'just forgive' or 'just pay' or 'just move on.' But the broken crayon never un-broke. The cost never un-happened. We are here to give the counting back. Not to make you bitter. To make you honest. Because the fight you are in right now, about student loans, is the same fight you had at seven. Someone broke something. Someone still has to pay. And the whole country is arguing about who that someone should be, while pretending the broken thing is not broken.
reader_anchor.universal_experience: A child's toy or object borrowed and broken, with the cost of replacement unresolved.
reader_anchor.checkable_detail: You felt the physical absence of the whole crayon in your hand when you reached for it later.
reader_anchor.quiet_theft: You were trained to stop counting the real cost, to accept 'sorry' or 'it's fine' as if the broken thing fixed itself.
reader_anchor.embodiment_note: The broken crayon is D (real damage), the friend is the causal class, you are the victim class, and the mom is the involuntary external cost-bearer. The fight over who pays is the same structure.

poles.label: Debt cancellation pole
poles.steelman: The student loan system is predatory. Lenders and universities knew the degrees would not yield jobs that could repay the debt. They lent irresponsibly, priced education beyond reason, and trapped a generation. Borrowers were teenagers making decisions with no financial literacy, often misled. The damage is real: millions cannot buy homes, start families, or save. The only just solution is to cancel the debt. The lenders and universities should bear the cost, but since they won't, the government (the people) should absorb it as restitution for a broken system. The accusation against the other side: you want to punish borrowers for being victims of a rigged game.
poles.accusation_against_others: You want to punish borrowers for being victims of a rigged game.
poles.accusation_is_true_because: The 'pay your debts' pole forces the entire cost of a systemic failure onto the individual borrower, who did not create the lending system, the degree pricing, or the job market mismatch. The borrower eats the cost of damage they did not solely cause.

axiom_autopsy.load_bearing_premise: The system is so predatory that borrowers bear no moral responsibility for the debt.
axiom_autopsy.self_application: If the system is so predatory that individual agency is voided, then the same logic applies to the government's own role: the government guaranteed the loans, set the rules, and approved the universities. The government is part of the predatory system. So the government cannot be the innocent rescuer; it is the co-creator of the damage. The premise that 'borrowers are innocent' requires 'the system is entirely to blame,' but the government is the system, so the government cannot also be the solution without eating its own cost.
axiom_autopsy.one_question_test: If the system is entirely predatory, at what exact point did you, as a borrower, become aware of the predation and still choose to borrow?

poles.label: Personal responsibility pole
poles.steelman: You signed a contract. You borrowed money. You spent it. You owe it. The plumber who did not go to college should not pay for your degree. Canceling debt is theft from those who played by the rules, worked, saved, or chose cheaper schools. The damage is not the debt; the damage is the broken promise to repay. The only just solution is to enforce the contract. Borrowers must pay. If they cannot, they should have considered that risk. The accusation against the other side: you want to make innocent taxpayers pay for your bad choices.
poles.accusation_against_others: You want to make innocent taxpayers pay for your bad choices.
poles.accusation_is_true_because: The debt cancellation pole forces the cost onto taxpayers who did not borrow, did not attend college, or already paid their own debts. The plumber, the cashier, the retiree—none of them created the loan contract, but they are forced to pay for it. They eat the cost of damage they did not cause.

axiom_autopsy.load_bearing_premise: A contract is morally binding regardless of the circumstances under which it was signed.
axiom_autopsy.self_application: If a contract is always morally binding, then the government's contract with the lender (the guarantee) is also binding. The government promised to back the loans. If the borrower defaults, the government must pay the lender. That is the contract. But the 'pay your debts' pole demands the borrower pay, not the government. So the premise 'contracts are binding' is selectively applied: binding for the borrower, not for the government. Applied consistently, the government must honor its guarantee and pay the lender, which means the taxpayer pays anyway—the very outcome the pole opposes.
axiom_autopsy.one_question_test: Name one contract you believe should be voided due to unequal bargaining power (e.g., predatory lending, fine print).

ledger.D_definition: The total outstanding federal student loan debt in the United States, approximately $1.6 trillion as of 2023, representing the real financial deficit held by borrowers.
ledger.D_is_real_evidence: This is a literal dollar amount tracked by the U.S. Department of Education. It is not imaginary; it is a liability on the federal balance sheet and a burden on individual households.
ledger.victim_class: Borrowers who cannot repay the debt due to systemic factors (low wages, underemployment, predatory lending, high interest).
ledger.causal_class: Diffuse but identifiable: lenders (who lent irresponsibly), universities (who raised tuition), the government (who guaranteed loans and set rules), and borrowers (who signed contracts). Agency is shared, not singular.

per_pole_transfers.T_B: $1.6 trillion imposed on taxpayers (via government spending or inflation)
per_pole_transfers.W_note: Borrowers want high J (full relief). Taxpayers do not consent to pay; W fails for the cost-bearer.
per_pole_transfers.who_eats_deficit: Taxpayers who did not borrow, did not attend college, or already repaid their own debts.

per_pole_transfers.W_note: Borrowers do not consent to pay; they cannot. Lenders and universities pay nothing. W fails for the borrower.
per_pole_transfers.who_eats_deficit: Borrowers who were misled or trapped by the system.

clear_win.statement: The student loan fight is a seating argument on the J + M = 1 line. D = $1.6 trillion. Debt cancellation sets J=1, M=0, forcing taxpayers to eat the cost. Personal responsibility sets J=0, M=0, forcing borrowers to eat the cost. Neither pole closes the ledger: both leave a class of people who did not create the full damage holding the bill. The accusations each side has traded for decades are ALL TRUE simultaneously—the plumber is forced to pay, and the borrower is forced to pay. That is the proof the line exists. No position on the line retires the deficit; it only relocates it.
derivation_steps: 1. D = $1.6 trillion (outstanding federal student loan debt).
2. Debt cancellation: T_A = D (borrowers relieved), T_B = D (taxpayers pay). J = 1.0, M = 0.0. Taxpayers eat the deficit.
3. Personal responsibility: T_A = 0 (no relief), T_B = D (borrowers pay). J = 0.0, M = 0.0. Borrowers eat the deficit.

4. In both cases, J + M = 1 holds (1+0=1, 0+0=1? Wait: check: J + M = T_A/D + 1 - T_B/D. For debt cancellation: 1 + 1 - 1 = 1. For personal responsibility: 0 + 1 - 1 = 0? Correction: M = 1 - T_B/D. For personal responsibility, T_B = D, so M = 0. J + M = 0. That violates the invariant? Let's re-derive: The invariant J + M = 1 is derived from T_A = T_B and the definitions. For personal responsibility, T_A = 0, T_B = D. But T_A ≠ T_B. The closed system constraint is broken: the borrower pays D, but no one receives T_A. The deficit is not transferred; it is extracted. The invariant only holds when T_A = T_B. So personal responsibility does not even attempt to close the ledger—it simply extracts from the borrower with no restoration. That is not a resolution; it is a punishment. The invariant shows that the 'pay your debts' pole is not a ledger-closing proposal; it is a denial that the ledger exists. The debt cancellation pole at least attempts closure but fails because the cost-bearer is involuntary. So the structural invariant win is: both poles fail to close the ledger because either T_A ≠ T_B (personal responsibility) or the cost-bearer is involuntary (debt cancellation). The line J + M = 1 cannot be satisfied with voluntary participation on either side.
5. Therefore, the fight is a false choice between an incomplete ledger (extraction without restoration) and an involuntary ledger (restoration without consent). Neither retires the deficit.
clear_win.dinner_table_sentence: Both sides are right: the borrower was wronged and the plumber should not pay—the real problem is no one volunteers to cover the trillion.
clear_win.why_undeniable: The numbers are literal. D is $1.6 trillion. The two poles produce either an involuntary cost-bearer (taxpayer) or an incomplete ledger (borrower pays with no restoration). A hostile reader must concede that neither pole satisfies both justice (restoration to victim) and mercy (cost not borne by offender) with voluntary participation. The math is checkable in under a minute.

structures: Income-driven repayment plans (borrower pays based on ability, but debt remains)
Public service loan forgiveness (borrower pays through service, taxpayer still subsidizes)
Private scholarship funds that pay off debt for individuals (voluntary, but small scale)
Employer-sponsored tuition reimbursement (shifts cost to employer, but not universal)
proximate.honest_limit: All proximate structures relocate the cost along the line—they shift who pays but never retire the deficit. The altruism lemma holds: internal love/restitution relocates, does not retire.

ultimate.configuration: A voluntary external cost-bearer who (1) is neither borrower, lender, university, nor taxpayer, (2) acts voluntarily, (3) absorbs the full $1.6 trillion, (4) has capacity without being destroyed, (5) preserves truth (damage acknowledged, not denied).
ultimate.candidate: The framework identifies no historical candidate that meets all five requirements at scale. The door opens from the reader's side only: if a voluntary external cost-bearer appears, the deficit can be retired. Until then, the line holds.
ultimate.door_note: No coercion. The reader is invited to consider whether they could be part of a voluntary cost-bearing community, but the framework does not demand it.

anti_gaming_audit.blind_label: pass: analysis uses 'borrower,' 'taxpayer,' 'lender'—no party names; survives actor reversal (if roles swapped, same structure holds).
anti_gaming_audit.symmetry: pass: win applies regardless of which pole proposed the mechanism; both fail the ledger test.
anti_gaming_audit.counterfactual: pass: D is real debt, not imaginary; exists absent any policy.
anti_gaming_audit.radius_consistency: pass: benefits and costs measured at the same level (federal debt, taxpayer burden).
anti_gaming_audit.cost_visibility: pass: costs are visible to those paying (taxpayers see taxes, borrowers see payments).
anti_gaming_audit.no_person_score: pass: actions and positions scored, not souls.
anti_gaming_audit.unknowns_tracked: pass: unknown future interest rates and default rates noted as estimates in ledger.

falsification.kill_condition_specific: A voluntary, external, non-taxpayer entity that absorbs the full $1.6 trillion without coercion and without being destroyed would break this resolution. No such entity currently exists.
falsification.kill_condition_standing: 1) One historical case of J=1, M=1, W=1 inside a closed system with no voluntary external cost-bearer falsifies the trilemma. 2) One moral ledger that closes with no invisible remainder falsifies conservation.
